bug_semantics: The authenticated /v1/completions endpoint accepted an outer list of text prompts or token-id prompts of attacker-chosen length. The serving path treated every outer-list element as a separate prompt, eagerly created one engine generator per element, merged all generators, and allocated per-prompt response state, so a single bounded-size HTTP control action could fan out into unbounded CPU, memory, scheduling, and engine-request work before any aggregate prompt-count budget was enforced.
flaw_origin: PR #2529 deliberately added batch completion support. Its first member commit d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 removed the immediate-parent guard that rejected len(prompts) > 1 and replaced the single engine.generate call with an unbounded for-loop over prompts, a generators list, merge_async_iterators(*generators), and response arrays sized by len(prompts), without adding an outer prompt-count limit. The second member only added type hints; squash landing 3a7dd7e367277c47472912e84375fa912df07328 preserved the flawed mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 shows author simon-mo <simon.mo@hey.com>, committer simon-mo <simon.mo@hey.com>, and the sole message 'Support Batch Completion in Server'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The assigned GHSA-87x5-vmc3-756j bundle identifies CVE-2026-73559, vulnerable pip versions >=0.19.0 and <0.26.0, patched version 0.26.0, PR #47845, and fix commit 675f4295cdfe0d870471c2b51bfeca3a68a9569e. The first-party advisory describes list[str] and list[list[int]] inputs reaching one engine generator and one response slot per rendered prompt.

PR #2529 ('Support Batch Completion in Server') states that it adds support for prompt as an array of strings or token arrays. git ls-remote resolves refs/pull/2529/head to a3a405c6a2b2f259671c5034c9a14e28187e97ac. git log from merge base 2709c0009aa434fbf2ef0fe48ca3094a2268b190 shows exactly two PR members: d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 ('Support Batch Completion in Server') followed by a3a405c6a2b2f259671c5034c9a14e28187e97ac ('Add type hint'). The GitHub squash landing is 3a7dd7e367277c47472912e84375fa912df07328.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep at 2709c0009aa434fbf2ef0fe48ca3094a2268b190 finds vllm/entrypoints/openai/serving_completion.py:236 raising 'Batching in completion API is not supported.' when len(prompts) > 1, and finds none of 'generators = []', 'for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts)', or 'merge_async_iterators'. At d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232, those vulnerable constructs appear at lines 269, 274, and 205/291 respectively, while the rejection is gone.

At the BIC, parse_prompt_format returns an outer list[str] or list[list[int]] unchanged as prompts; create_completion then enumerates every prompt, tokenizes it, appends self.engine.generate(..., f'{request_id}-{i}', ...) to generators, merges all generators, passes num_prompts=len(prompts) to streaming state, and allocates final_res_batch with len(prompts). No outer count check precedes these allocations.

Release ancestry: v0.19.0 resolves to 2a69949bdadf0e8942b7a1619b229cb475beef20 and merge-base(3a7dd7e367277c47472912e84375fa912df07328, v0.19.0) equals the squash landing, so the decomposed BIC was landed before the declared affected range. It was already landed by v0.3.0, which is consistent with (and earlier than) the bundle's conservative >=0.19.0 lower bound. v0.19.0 source still contains completion/serving.py:203 merge_async_iterators(*generators).

Patched boundary: v0.25.0 resolves to 702f4814fe54fabff350d43cb753ae3e47c0c276; merge-base with fix 675f4295cdfe0d870471c2b51bfeca3a68a9569e is 6db31c8e76f5458177be0d716cca758e51fa2f65, and git grep finds no VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS in its completion protocol or envs.py. v0.26.0 resolves to 568afb3a13806beb53bb2e6bd518269357b237c0; its merge-base with the fix is the fix itself, and its source contains VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS validation in completion/protocol.py and the default/configuration in envs.py.

Fix commit 675f4295cdfe0d870471c2b51bfeca3a68a9569e (parent d99adcebdc9402c26346230ef2480d1cb72e654e) adds a before-model validator that distinguishes a flat token-id prompt from outer prompt lists and rejects prompt or prompt_embeds lists above VLLM_MAX_COMPLETION_PROMPTS before renderer preprocessing and generator allocation; it also adds the configurable default limit of 1024 and regression coverage for both text and token-id prompt lists.

BIC-only attribution check: the raw d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232 commit object has matching human author and committer identities and no trailers or body beyond its title. No PR-body statement, later refactor, or fix metadata was used for AI attribution.
reasoning: The request schema's list forms were not sufficient to create this denial-of-service while the serving layer rejected more than one parsed prompt. The causal transition is therefore the first PR #2529 member, d04fd49c2bc9540237d3d11b6d1de26bbc35d232: relative to its immediate parent it removes that rejection and introduces the complete unbounded fan-out path. The later type-hint member and mainline squash are not smaller origins, so the squash was decomposed and the first member is the BIC. Direct inspection of parent and child trees proves immediate-parent absence. Mainline ancestry and source checks prove that the mechanism is present by v0.19.0, while the referenced direct fix is absent from v0.25.0 and included in v0.26.0 with the new pre-fan-out bound. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for attribution; it contains a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
